stem: During the germination of barley seeds, amylase is produced.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the sequence of events that lead to the production of amylase during germination of barley seeds.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Malting is a process involved in the production of a drink called beer. During malting, barley seed germination is controlled so that the sugars produced during germination can be used in the production of beer.

Fig. 3.1 shows two features of a germinating barley seed during the first five days of malting:
• activity of the amylase enzyme
• the percentage of starch reserves remaining in the barley seed.

starch reserves
amylase activity

parts.text: State the precise location of the starch reserves in the barley seed.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 3.1, describe **and** explain the effect of malting on amylase activity and the percentage of starch reserves remaining in the germinated barley seed.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
In the malting process, germination is stopped before the concentration of sugars in the germinating barley seeds exceeds a concentration that causes shoot or root growth.

Drying the germinating barley seeds at $50^\circ\text{C}$ is one method used to stop malting.
parts.text: Explain how this method would stop malting.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why malting is stopped before shoot or root growth occurs.
